name: Ford - BlueOval SK Battery Park, Glendale KY
type: Battery Manufacturing Plant (JV with SK On)

fieldNotes.site: BlueOval SK Battery Park, Glendale (Hardin County) KY - a Ford / SK On joint-venture EV battery campus on the Glendale Megasite, two ~4M sq ft battery plant buildings (~8M sq ft combined). Roster coordinates (37.6017,-85.9055) point at Glendale town center, ~2.4 km NW of the actual plant. Corrected center to ~37.5860,-85.8800 (the white-roof dual-plant complex) confirmed by satellite: two giant battery plant buildings sit immediately west of I-65, with employee parking lots full of cars on the west side and process/utility structures (tank farms, conveyor bridges) at the south. Production officially began Aug 2025; Ford announced the workforce would be idled by Feb 2026 with rehire planned for 2027 after retooling - so the plant is operational but currently in a retooling pause.
fieldNotes.imagery: Available Maxar/Airbus satellite tiles capture the site during the active construction / early-ramp phase: surrounding ground is largely bare graded dirt and construction laydown, so the final operational truck-yard, drop-yard and gate configuration is NOT fully built out in imagery. Most layout/count fields are therefore low-confidence estimates and flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Marked true (low confidence). Chain-link perimeter fencing is clearly visible along the public perimeter road in 2025-08 Street View; a megasite battery plant of this security profile (JV with valuable IP, hazmat) operates controlled gated truck access. The exact gate structure could not be positively resolved in construction-era imagery.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Marked true (low confidence) - a secured automotive-JV battery campus of this scale conventionally operates a staffed gatehouse at the main entrance. A booth structure was not positively resolved; flagged uncertain. remoteGs false as a consequence.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Marked true (low confidence) - two separate ~4M sq ft plant buildings each with their own dock banks on different faces; raw-material receiving and finished-cell shipping would run from physically distinct dock clusters.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Estimated 25-50 across the two large plant buildings; regular bay rhythm visible along the SW building's south/west faces in z18-z19 imagery. Exact count obscured by roof angle and construction state - flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Banded 10-25; a paved truck/trailer staging area is visible toward the south of the complex but much of the surrounding area is still construction laydown - flagged uncertain. dropYard true.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: True - two enormous separate plant buildings plus multiple process/utility support structures form a single campus.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur into the property could be identified; the CSX line corridor is some distance away. railServed false.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Glendale is a small rural Hardin County community surrounded by farmland; the megasite is greenfield development off I-65. Rural.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: True (low confidence) - the megasite has vast unused paved/graded width around the entrance, ample physical room for express/bypass lanes.
fieldNotes.geofence: perimeter box covers the developed/fenced plant complex core (~740 acres); the broader Glendale Megasite parcel is larger (~1,500+ acres). Sub-zones are best-effort estimates from construction-era imagery.
